title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook documents the canonical structure and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation focused on SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. The goal is a single reference that helps authors, reviewers, and on-call engineers create consistent, high-quality docs that reduce developer friction and support load.

Scope and audience

- Primary audience: SDK writers, developer advocates, solutions engineers, support triage, and product engineers.
- Scope: All public-facing and internal SDK guides, quickstarts, API example snippets, docs-site editorial/ops processes, and the canonical list of top support issues for the Redwood Inference API/SDK surface.

Owner and review cadence

- Document owner: eng-developer-experience team (contact: Aisha Patel).
- Reviewers: see metadata.
- Review cadence: major review every quarter; micro-review (typo/patch) on every release or hotfix.

Standards for SDK Guides (required structure)

Every SDK guide must follow this structure to ensure consistency:

1. Title and short summary (1-2 lines)
2. Supported versions and compatibility matrix
3. Quickstart (copy-paste runnable)
4. API reference (examples for common routes)
5. Error handling and retry guidance
6. Performance tips (batching, streaming, concurrency)
7. Troubleshooting (link to top support issues)
8. Changelog and authorship

Example header (first lines in every guide):

Title: Redwood Python SDK — Text Generation
Summary: Quick, production-aware guide to calling the text generation endpoint with the Redwood Python SDK.

Quickstart (Python) — copy-paste runnable\n
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"${REDWOOD_API_KEY}\")
resp = client.generate(model=\"redwood/gptx-1\", prompt=\"Write a concise summary of Redwood Inference.\", max_tokens=120)
print(resp.text)
```

Quickstart (curl)

```bash
curl -sS \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood/gptx-1\",\"prompt\":\"Hello from Redwood\",\"max_tokens\":40}' \
  https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
```

API Examples: patterns & conventions

- Use small, focused examples that demonstrate one concept each (auth, streaming, function calling, embeddings).
- Prefer the official SDK snippet first, then the raw HTTP/curl example.
- Include expected response shape and status codes for each example.

Common API examples to include in every SDK package:

- Authentication and environment variables
- Simple text generation (sync and streaming)
- Chat-style conversations (stateful prompt + KV cache hint)
- Embeddings and vector storage example (with recommended batch sizes)
- Error handling and idempotency tokens for retries

Docs-site operating procedures (publishing workflow)

1. Author creates or updates doc in the drafts branch of the docs repo and references this playbook.
2. Run docs linting (pre-commit + markdownlint) and unit examples (CI job that executes code snippets).
3. Submit PR to eng-developer-experience/docs with a short description and test logs.
4. At least one reviewer from DevEx and one from Product must approve for docs that change public contract or examples.
5. After merge, CI deploys to staging docs site. Author performs a smoke test (verify samples run, code blocks render, and links resolve).
6. Schedule a release to production docs during a non-peak window (recommended Mon-Thu, 02:00-06:00 UTC for global audience) or with a rollout note if the change is high-impact.

Editorial checklist (must be completed before publish):

- [ ] Title and summary present and concise
- [ ] Quickstart verified (copy/paste)
- [ ] SDK snippet included first, then curl/HTTP
- [ ] Supported versions and migration notes included
- [ ] Labels/tags added for searchability (see tagging table below)
- [ ] Related_pages links set
- [ ] Tests for code snippets passed in CI

Tagging and metadata conventions

Use these labels to improve search and filtering on the docs site:

| Label | Use case | Examples |
|-------|----------|----------|
| sdk | SDK-specific guides | python-sdk, js-sdk |
| quickstart | Short onboarding guides | onboarding, hello-world |
| api-examples | HTTP/curl examples & patterns | generate, chat, embeddings |
| template | Reusable templates | sdk-template, quickstart-template |
| troubleshooting | Known issues & fixes | top-support-issues |

Quickstarts & Templates (canonical set)

We maintain a set of lightweight templates authors must use to reduce duplicate effort:

- Quickstart template (1 page): 1 heading, 1 short summary, 3-step copy-paste quickstart, 1 troubleshooting pointer, 2 links to SDK reference.
- SDK Guide template (multi-page): follow SDK standard structure above.
- API Examples gallery: catalog of small runnable patterns (each pattern is 1 standalone page).
- Troubleshooting card template: symptom, likely causes, canonical fix, telemetry/diagnostic commands, escalation path.

Template example: Quickstart (Hello Generation)

1. Prerequisites: API key, Python 3.10+, pip install redwood==1.4.0
2. Quick command: pip install redwood
3. Copy-paste snippet (see Quickstart above)

Performance and production guidance (short list to include in every SDK guide)

- Use batching for embeddings: recommended batch size 64-256 depending on GPU memory.
- Prefer streaming for low-latency token-by-token workloads; use concurrency limits on the client side.
- Cache prefixes and reuse session tokens for multi-turn conversations to reduce token costs.
- For latency SLOs <150ms 95th percentile, use dedicated capacity or pinned models.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage-first list)

1. Authentication errors (401/403)
   - Symptom: API returns 401 or 403 when calling endpoints.
   - Likely causes: invalid/missing API key, incorrect header format, expired key scope.
   - Canonical fix: Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY env var set; show exact curl test:

   curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" \
        https://api.redwood.dev/v1/health

   - If key is valid but scoped incorrectly, instruct to request new key via console or contact support.

2. Rate limit errors (429)
   - Symptom: 429 responses under load.
   - Likely causes: client burst behavior, missing exponential backoff, shared API key usage.
   - Canonical fix: Implement exponential backoff + jitter (example pseudo-code):

   ```python
   import time, random
   def retry_with_backoff(fn, retries=5):
       for i in range(retries):
           try:
               return fn()
           except RateLimitError:
               sleep = (2 ** i) + random.random()
               time.sleep(sleep)
       raise
   ```

3. Incorrect model output or hallucination
   - Symptom: Model returns incorrect facts or unsafe text.
   - Likely causes: prompt engineering issues, insufficient context, model selection.
   - Canonical fix: Add verification step, use model with stronger factuality profile, add post-processing filters. Provide an eval prompt set and link to quality-guardrails doc.

4. Streaming broken / incomplete chunks
   - Symptom: Client receives partial streaming events and then disconnects.
   - Likely causes: client-side streaming handling, proxy timeouts, chunk decoding errors.
   - Canonical fix: Verify chunk decoding logic, use chunk buffering heuristics, increase proxy timeouts (Nginx/gateway: proxy_read_timeout 120s). Example Node fetch handler pattern provided in the SDK template.

5. Embedding throughput poor / OOM
   - Symptom: Out-of-memory on client or server when batching embeddings.
   - Likely causes: batch size too large for model/hardware, data pipeline memory leak.
   - Canonical fix: Reduce batch size, stream vectors to persistent store, monitor GPU memory. Add a small YAML config example for recommended batch sizes: 

```yaml
embedding:
  batch_size_recommended: \"128\"
  batch_size_max: \"512\"
  io_chunk_size: \"4096\"
```

Troubleshooting runbook (quick triage steps)

1. Reproduce locally with curl and the same API key. If reproducible, capture request/response and request-id header.
2. Check service status page and any ongoing incidents.
3. If 5xx, collect logs, full request payload, and the request-id; escalate to eng-sre.
4. If rate-limited, confirm client throttling and apply backoff.
5. For model quality issues, run a short eval harness against a known prompt set and compare outputs between model variants.

Escalation matrix

- Level 1 (Support): triage, reproduce, provide workaround (30 min target).
- Level 2 (DevEx / SDK owner): fix docs, update examples, code patch if sample SDK bug (4 hour target).
- Level 3 (Eng-SRE / Runtime team): investigate infra, kernel, or model-serving defects (SLA-driven).

Canonical fixes repository and CI requirements

- All canonical fixes (code snippets that are recommended as fixes) must be stored in the docs repo under /examples/canonical-fixes and have unit tests in CI that execute them weekly.
- Any code change to SDK examples must include a test that runs the snippet against a sandbox environment and asserts expected response shape.

Appendix: Example API Patterns

1) Chat with function calling (Python SDK)

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"$REDWOOD_API_KEY\")
resp = client.chat(
    model=\"redwood/chatx-1\",
    messages=[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"You are concise.\"}, {\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Create a JSON schema for a meeting note.\"}],
    functions=[{\"name\":\"create_meeting\",\"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"title\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"date\":{\"type\":\"string\",\"format\":\"date\"}}}}]
print(resp)
```

2) Embeddings batching (Node.js)

```js
const Redwood = require('redwood');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
async function embedBatch(items){
  const batches = chunk(items, 128);
  for(const b of batches){
    const resp = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'redwood/embed-1', input: b });
    // persist resp to vector DB
  }
}
```

Contact and feedback

- For doc-related incidents or missing examples open a ticket in the DevEx JIRA project (DE-xxx) and tag eng-developer-experience.
- For urgent production-facing doc errors (broken code or incorrect API contract) escalate to Level 2 and notify #devex on Slack.

Related resources

- eng-developer-experience docs playbook (internal)
- quality-guardrails and eval-harness pages for model QA
- API reference and SDK repositories

This playbook is the canonical reference for DevEx docs related to SDKs, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operations, and the top support issues. Authors should link back to this page from any template or quickstart they publish.
